frameworks.name: Video Production Workflow Decomposition
frameworks.definition: A systematic decomposition of video creation into granular task-level workflows (idea research → ranking → cross-listing → scripting → outlining → packaging) that can be automated or delegated.

claims.text: Organizations must shift from role-based hiring (filling org chart holes with a 'position' like 'editor') to workflow-based thinking that decomposes every function into granular actions.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: organizations scaling via AI and automation
claims.mechanism: Role-based thinking masks the actual work decomposition; workflow-based thinking exposes repeatable steps that can be automated by AI agents.

claims.text: At Acquisition.com, media output tripled in the last month without increasing headcount because AI agents handle 30-50% of granular task-level work.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Granular task decomposition creates discrete jobs that AI agents can execute; one person can now do work of three, five, then ten by layering agent automation.

numbers.axis: productivity multiplier and AI workload coverage

anchors.value: one person output work of three, five, ten

claims.text: In training and implementation, explaining theory and psychology behind actions slows comprehension and retention; telling people only what actions to take compresses training time and increases adherence.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Reducing word-to-action translation distance lowers cognitive load, raising comprehension and behavioral stickiness; theory adds delay without improving execution.

claims.text: Service business founders claiming productization is blocked by their own delivery are actually facing a workflow decomposition problem that AI agents can now solve.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Reframing bottleneck from 'I must deliver everything' to 'I must decompose and assign each step' enables delegation and automation.

claims.text: A fund-launch consulting business at $4M revenue (3-3.5M from fund launch services, 1M from CFO services) is bottlenecked by founder inability to delegate delivery, solvable by documenting SOPs and productizing the service.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Documented SOPs and workflow automation remove founder dependency, freeing the founder for business development and strategic work.
bounded_by: applies to service businesses with high-touch delivery

examples.text: Video production is decomposed into discrete steps: (1) idea conception requiring trend research, (2) ranking of trend fit and brand alignment, (3) scripting with outline, hook, stories, and proof elements, (4) packaging. When an editor is told 'go make a YouTube video,' they may know some steps but lack clear directions for each. By breaking the entire production into granular levels, each step becomes a discrete job that either a team member executes or an AI agent automates.

practices.text: Break down all business tasks to granular action-level steps rather than keeping them as role-level or project-level abstractions.
When training team members or GPs, focus on telling them what actions to take, not why or the theory behind the actions.
For each granular workflow step, create clear directions and assign ownership or automation rather than leaving steps implicit.
Document SOPs and productize services to remove founder dependency and enable scaling.
